prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: a high-fidelity full-page desktop homepage design exploration, one complete page per image. This is a fresh art-directed visual concept for the Ferramenta family of Rust libraries. The request is a holistic design direction, including the tables, content hierarchy, typography and overall composition.

Preserve the approved brand idea: warm, light, refined precision engineering, satin steel and a restrained oxide accent. The reference instrument must have a meaningful relationship to the library. Use ONE substantial object illustration in the hero only, never a wall of product photos below it. Preserve useful editorial content and technical evidence. Keep everything light-theme-only with a clean warm-white reading ground (#FCFCFA or white), graphite text (#2D3632), readable secondary ink (#5C665E), and a measured oxide accent (#8C4D30).

Critical current request: all decorative section backgrounds have been rejected. NO material background strips, gradients in section grounds, grain on the page, wave edges, diagonal section shapes, foggy fade-outs or dark sections. Materials belong in the actual hero object and small supplied product symbol only. Create variety through the composition, type, hierarchy, reading measures, examples, charts and table design, not by adding background treatments. No decorative horizontal separators between stories. Tables may have functional rules, but must be intentionally designed rather than copied from a generic UI kit.

The whole page must breathe: wide column gutters, approximately 120–160px desktop separation between major stories, readable body leading around 1.6–1.75, and clear space around table captions, notes and next actions. This is a complete homepage with interesting lower content, not a huge hero plus a sparse feature grid. Avoid both giant blank wastelands and compressed tiny copy. Use around 5 considered content moments plus a modest footer. No fake testimonials, invented usage statistics or unsupported API claims.

Output ONE full-page desktop website comp approximately 1200px wide by 2800–3400px tall, head-on and uncropped, no browser frame, presentation board, side-by-side variants or annotations outside the web page. All visible website text in US English. Follow the product copy and exact numeric data supplied below; the text files remain the accuracy authority. The object reference has alpha: do not bring a black backdrop from the image viewer into the design.

Direction: Working specimen
Make the complete homepage feel like a beautifully typeset practical instrument handbook. The hero keeps the large product title and the reference metal object, but is shallower than the editorial folio, so the first working specimen appears early. After it, compose two or three large worked figures at DIFFERENT widths, separated by real reading paragraphs and compact margin annotations. A narrow left text rail carries meaningful section titles such as Rendering, Output policy, Measurements, or Compatibility, Scanner, Measurements; never decorative numbers. The specimen itself is the layout's anchor: source and output have a carefully aligned baseline, with a restrained mechanical annotation in oxide showing the meaningful transformation or next-match location. This is flat, readable typesetting on white, not a dashboard of cards.
Reinvent the tables as specimen ledgers: visually group a field label, its concrete example and the relevant constraint. For Ferroni's scanner, use an aligned three-step byte-position ledger alongside the source line, clearly preserving all pattern indexes and byte ranges; for the feature matrix, give the feature names ample space and align compact Yes/No columns. For Ferromark, let the Rust and Node.js output policies form two readable three-column cases. The benchmark presentation must still preserve its denominator, dates and caveats. No spreadsheet grid, shaded header, zebra stripes, many outline boxes or chip cloud. A very clear regular-width engineering sans, slightly narrower low-weight headings, and compact mono only in executable specimens create the character. The precision comes from alignment and useful annotation, not texture, grids over the page or decorative fine rules. Use a wide closing note and a modest installation line.

Reference roles: Image 1 is the completed Ferromark sibling homepage in this exact direction. Use it for a coherent family identity: matching typography, table language, header/footer, editorial rhythm and level of precision. It is a STYLE AND COMPOSITION reference, not the product content to copy. Image 2 is Ferroni's meaningful pattern comparator: three parallel pattern cassettes and a scanning pointer. Replace the sibling's document instrument with this object in the hero. Image 3 is Ferroni's existing product symbol, used small with the Ferroni wordmark. Do not show Ferromark's document leaves, name or benchmark figures on the Ferroni page. Adapt the reading order to the actual scanner and regex story rather than mechanically repeating all blocks.

Product content:
Header: Ferroni. Overview. Start with Rust. Scanner. Benchmarks. GitHub. The Ferramenta family.
Hero title: Ferroni.
Purpose headline: Oniguruma regex, in memory-safe Rust.
Hero description: Run familiar patterns, from lookbehind to recursion, and the scanner that syntax highlighters drive.
Primary action: Start with Rust. Secondary action: Explore the scanner.

Working example title: See what the pattern finds.
Pattern: (?<=item-)\d+
Text: item-104  item-208
Matches: 104, 208

Opening story: Patterns carry a contract.
Existing grammars and applications depend on how lookbehind, captured text, Unicode properties and recursive patterns behave. Rewriting the expression can change that behavior just as surely as changing the engine.
Ferroni continues Oniguruma's expressive syntax in Rust. Choose it when that compatibility matters: an editor grammar, a highlighter, or a search that depends on a feature the regex crate deliberately leaves out.
Selected syntax checks, not a blanket compatibility score.
Exact feature table columns: Feature | Ferroni | Rust regex.
Rows: Lookahead and lookbehind | Yes | No.
Backreferences | Yes | No.
Unicode character properties | Yes | Yes.

Worked scanner figure: One line. Several patterns. The next match.
A TextMate grammar asks which pattern matches next from a position in the line. The scanner returns the leftmost match, its pattern index and capture ranges. The tokenizer resumes at the previous match's end.
Source: const answer = 42 // note
Pattern indexes: 0 keywords, 1 strings, 2 comments, 3 numbers.
Exact ledger columns: Resume at byte | Next match | Pattern index | Byte range.
Rows: 0 | const | 0 | 0..5.
5 | 42 | 3 | 15..17.
17 | // note | 2 | 18..25.
Note: Regular scanner offsets are bytes; explicit UTF-16 methods support editor text models.
Link: Understand the scanner.

Continuation: Continued with care.
Oniguruma's C project ended in April 2025. Ferroni continues the engine in Rust, with compatibility checks against the original. Rust's regex crate makes a different tradeoff: it leaves out lookaround and backreferences for predictable linear-time searching.

Evidence figure title: Reuse changes the picture.
Ferroni throughput relative to each comparator; higher is faster.
Exact table columns: Comparator | macOS ARM64 | Linux x86-64.
C Oniguruma | 3.44× | 2.75×.
PCRE2 JIT | 0.70× | 0.63×.
Provenance: Steady reuse. 21 tasks per pair. 513 corpus inputs. October 15, 2026. Revision 1c8d45f. Blacksmith VMs, macOS ARM64 and Linux x86-64.
Caveats: C Oniguruma compiles patterns faster. PCRE2 JIT remains faster in the steady-reuse aggregates shown here. Every task checks expected output before timing. These are isolated regex steps, not whole-application benchmarks.
Link: Read the complete benchmarks.

Closing story: Put a boundary around the work.
Memory safety does not make every pattern cheap. Choose retry budgets and supported time limits for untrusted input. Browser WebAssembly uses retry limits instead of timeouts. Reuse compiled patterns where the workload allows it.
Install: cargo add ferroni.
Footer: Ferroni. Part of Ferramenta. GitHub. Imprint. Privacy.
